questions.prompt: "Waiting on the sponsor's parts order" is holding up five different tasks across the project. What should you use?
questions.explanation: A blocker is a reusable, project-scoped reason that can be attached to many tasks at once. Resolving it once detaches it from every task and recomputes each of their statuses. A dependency is the wrong tool — it links exactly two tasks.

answers.text: A blocker, attached to all five tasks
Five dependencies pointing at one placeholder task
A comment on each of the five tasks

questions.prompt: You attach a blocker to a task that is currently IN_PROGRESS. What happens to its status?
questions.explanation: Attaching a blocker forces the task to BLOCKED. It returns to TODO only once it has no open blockers and no unfinished dependencies — the system will not silently leave it looking active while it is stuck.

answers.text: It stays IN_PROGRESS with a warning icon

questions.prompt: Where do you go to see a project's milestones?
questions.explanation: The Gantt view. Milestones are dates drawn against the timeline, alongside the bars for the work that has to land before them. The task board is organised by status, not by time, so it cannot show you a commitment at all.

answers.text: The Gantt view, where each one is a marker on the timeline
The task board, as a fifth column after Done
The dashboard, under your assigned tasks
The Reports tab, in the activity log

questions.prompt: A milestone's date has passed and the work in front of it is still open. What's the right response?
questions.explanation: Look at what's still there, and either finish the work or move the date deliberately. A date nobody has moved and nobody has met stops carrying information for everyone who reads the timeline.

answers.text: Either finish the remaining work or move the date on purpose
Delete it and create a fresh one so the timeline looks clean
Leave it — it will clear itself on the next nightly refresh
Unlink the unfinished tasks from it

questions.prompt: Tasks and milestones are the same kind of object — a milestone is just a task with a later date.
questions.explanation: False. A milestone has no work of its own; it is a date the club has committed to, and the tasks are what has to land before it. That is why they are drawn on the timeline rather than sitting in a board column.
